title: Small coherent colimits generated by coproducts and pushouts
statement: Use quasicategories, mapping spaces, coherent functors and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory in a larger universe. Then $\mathcal C$ admits colimits of every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial diagram if and only if it admits all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts (including the empty coproduct) and all pushouts. If $\mathcal C$ has these colimits and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is any coherent functor to a quasicategory in a sufficiently large universe, then $F$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits if and only if it preserves all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts and all pushouts. In the preservation assertion, saying that $F$ preserves a colimit includes existence of the corresponding colimit of the image diagram in $\mathcal D$. Neither local $\mathcal U$-smallness nor presentability is assumed.

source.place: Duals of Theorem 7.3.22 and Proposition 7.3.23, printed p. 356 (PDF p. 371). No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical existence and preservation theorem. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Assume that $\mathcal C$ has $\mathcal U$-small coproducts, including the empty one, and pushouts. When proving preservation also fix $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving those coproducts and pushouts, with existence in $\mathcal D$ for the image diagrams. Work in a universe $\mathcal V$ containing $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal D$ and all functor categories used below; no mapping space is required to be $\mathcal U$-small. For a diagram $p:H\to\mathcal E$, write $E_H^{\mathcal E}(p,t)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_Ht)$. The cocone criterion says that a particular cocone $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Hc$ is colimiting precisely when composition with $\lambda$ gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,t)\simeq E_H^{\mathcal E}(p,t)$ for every $t$. In the following steps all equivalences of cocone spaces are natural in $t$, so they test the actual induced cocones, not only their apices.

source.place: Proofs of Theorem 7.3.22 and Corollary 7.3.17, enlargement of the ambient universe; dual mapping-space argument.

proof.text: Colimits are closed under $\mathcal U$-small disjoint unions of indexing shapes: if $p$ is a diagram on $\coprod_{i\in I}H_i$ and each restriction has colimit $c_i$, then $\coprod_i c_i$ with the component cocones is a colimit. Indeed a coherent transformation on the disjoint union is precisely an independent transformation on every $H_i$, in every simplicial degree. Hence $E_{\coprod H_i}(p,t)=\prod_iE_{H_i}(p|_{H_i},t)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(c_i,t)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\coprod_i c_i,t)$, and the composite is induced by that cocone. For $I=\varnothing$ this is the initial-object universal property. If $F$ preserves the component colimit cocones and their coproduct, the identical calculation in $\mathcal D$ proves that it preserves this disjoint-union colimit cocone.

source.place: Disjoint-union closure in the dual of Theorem 7.3.22; the argument is directly the coproduct and cocone definitions.

proof.text: For a pushout $H=B\amalg_A D$ of indexing simplicial sets with $A\to D$ degreewise injective, use [lem-coef-infinity-colimit-gluing]. If the three restricted diagrams have colimits $x,y,z$ (on $B,A,D$ respectively), it constructs the coherent span $x\leftarrow y\to z$ and identifies its pushout, with the induced cocone, as a colimit on $H$. Thus our hypotheses give the colimit on $H$. This construction also proves preservation in the cases needed here: applying $F$ to the three partial colimit cocones and to their comparison data gives comparison maps for the image cocones; the contractible-choice assertion of the cited node identifies them with the image assembly. If $F$ preserves the three partial cocones and the pushout span, the same cited statement in $\mathcal D$ says that the image of the induced cocone is colimiting. Contractibility retains the comparison homotopies, so this verifies the image cocone itself.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.4.2.2 and Remark 4.4.2.3, printed p.296; compatibility of the induced comparison maps.

proof.text: Let $N=N(\mathbb N)$ and let $S\subseteq N$ be the simplicial subset generated by all vertices and the consecutive edges $n\to n+1$, with degeneracies. By [lem-coef-infinity-sequential-spine], restriction along $S\hookrightarrow N$ induces, for every coherent $q:N\to\mathcal E$ and every $t\in\mathcal E$, a natural equivalence $$E_N(q,t)\simeq E_S(q|_S,t).$$ The same node states naturality in $q,t$, compatibility with postcomposition by coherent functors, and that a specified cocone is colimiting exactly when its restriction is. Thus this restriction equivalence can be used in both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ without assuming any sequential colimit or local smallness.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 7.3.17, consecutive-edge spine of the natural-number nerve; expanded using finite spines and increasing-union mapping-space descent.

proof.text:
We now construct all sequential colimits and prove that $F$ preserves them. Given $q:N(\mathbb N)\to\mathcal C$, write $x_n=q(n)$ and $f_n:x_n\to x_{n+1}$. The spine $S$ of step 4 is the simplicial pushout of the disjoint union of its consecutive edges and its discrete vertex set along the disjoint union of the two endpoints of each edge. The endpoint-to-edge map is a monomorphism; this pushout description follows degreewise since the only nondegenerate simplices of $S$ are its listed vertices and edges. On an edge, the colimit is its target $x_{n+1}$ by [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit], with source leg $f_n$ and target leg the identity. Steps 2 and 3 therefore give a colimit $P$ for $q|_S$ by the pushout
$$P=\left(\coprod_{n\geq0}x_n\right)\amalg_{\coprod_{n\geq0}(x_n\amalg x_{n+1})}\left(\coprod_{n\geq0}x_{n+1}\right).$$
On the middle summand $x_n\amalg x_{n+1}$ the first map consists of the two vertex inclusions; the second has components $f_n$ and $1_{x_{n+1}}$. The equivalence $E_N(q,P)\to E_S(q|_S,P)$ of step 4 is surjective on connected components: choose a coherent cocone $\lambda$ on $q$ and a path from its restricted cocone to the constructed spine cocone. Naturality in $t$ and this path identify the composition map for $\lambda$, up to homotopy, with the equivalence for the spine, so $\lambda$ is colimiting by step 1. Every operation constructing $P$ is a countable coproduct, a binary coproduct or a pushout, and the edge colimit cocones are preserved by any functor, again by the final-vertex formula. Thus steps 2 and 3 show that $F$ sends the spine cocone to a colimit cocone. Step 4 in $\mathcal D$, and its compatibility with postcomposition, then prove that the image of $\lambda$ is colimiting as well: the chosen path is carried to a path between its restriction and the image spine cocone, so the same natural mapping-space test applies. No general sequential colimit theorem has been assumed.

source.place: Dual of Corollary 7.3.17 and its displayed formula (7.3.17.2), printed pp.354-355; coproduct-pushout construction with the spine comparison from step 4.

proof.text: Prove by induction on $d\geq-1$ that every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set of dimension at most $d$ indexes colimits in $\mathcal C$, and that $F$ preserves these colimit cocones. Dimension at most $-1$ means the empty set, treated in step 2. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow H$. At stage $d\geq0$ it expresses the $d$-skeleton as the pushout of its $(d-1)$-skeleton and $\coprod_{\sigma}\Delta^d$ over $\coprod_{\sigma}\partial\Delta^d$, where $\sigma$ ranges over the nondegenerate $d$-simplices of $H$. This set is $\mathcal U$-small. The boundary $\partial\Delta^d$ has dimension at most $d-1$ (and is empty for $d=0$), so the induction hypothesis gives its restricted colimits and their preservation. Each diagram on $\Delta^d$ has colimit its last vertex, with the specified cocone in [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit]; applying $F$ gives the same last-vertex cocone in $\mathcal D$. Step 2 handles both disjoint unions. Step 3 applies because the coproduct of boundary inclusions is degreewise injective. It constructs the colimit on the new skeleton and proves its preservation. If $H$ has dimension at most $d$, this skeleton is $H$, completing the induction. No bound on the number of simplices within the fixed dimension is used.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.4.2.6, bounded-dimension induction, and Proposition 4.4.2.7, printed pp.296-297; relative skeletal filtration as in Kerodon 0077. The indexing attachment alone is also Stacks 018R, simplicial.tex, lemma-glue-simplex.

proof.text: For arbitrary $\mathcal U$-small $K$, [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] applied to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ gives an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional skeleta with union $K$. They and the indexing nerve $N(\mathbb N)$ are $\mathcal U$-small. Fix any $p:K\to\mathcal C$. Step 6 supplies colimit cocones $\lambda_n$ on all the restricted diagrams, including the empty initial stage. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-directed-union-local-colimits] to obtain a coherent sequence $q$ of their apices, retaining the restriction comparison data. Step 5 supplies a colimit cocone on $q$. The directed-union node identifies its induced cocone on $p$ as colimiting, proving existence for every $K$. For preservation, step 6 says that every $F\lambda_n$ is colimiting; the postcomposition clause of the directed-union node says that $Fq$ with the image data is an assembly of $Fp$. Step 5 says that the image of the colimit cocone on $q$ is colimiting on $Fq$. Applying the cocone correspondence in $\mathcal D$ now proves that the image of the constructed cocone on $p$ is colimiting. Any other colimiting cocone on $p$ is equivalent to this one in its cocone category; the initial-object and componentwise-equivalence assertions of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] show that its image is also colimiting. This proves preservation of all the stated colimits, with existence only for the corresponding image diagrams in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.3.22, countable skeletal union, and Proposition 7.3.23; HTT Proposition 4.4.2.6-7 and Corollary 4.2.3.10. The partial-colimit assembly is invoked without global cocompleteness.

proof.text: Conversely, a discrete simplicial set indexed by any $\mathcal U$-small set is $\mathcal U$-small, including the empty one, and the nerve of the three-object span category is finite. Its colimits are respectively the coproducts and pushouts by definition. Thus existence of all $\mathcal U$-small colimits gives the asserted coproducts and pushouts; preservation of all such colimit cocones implies preservation of these particular ones. Together with steps 2-7 this proves both equivalences. The construction uses only $\mathcal U$-small coproduct indices and the countable skeletal tower; the auxiliary universe was used for testing mapping spaces, not to assume extra colimits.
